groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Good morning and welcome to People in the News. With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines.
W: Hi, Brian. Thanks for having me today. I'm excited to explain to the audience what my book is really about.
M: Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal.
W: I'm aware of those claims, but they simply aren't true. People who haven't read the book are making assumptions about my arguments. They know I'm a vegetarian, that I don't wear leather or fur, and that I always use public transportation. So they're depicting me as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist determined to force my beliefs on others.
M: But don't you want others to adopt your practices? You've campaigned for animal rights and the environment for decades.
W: I'd love it if people choose to live as I do. But my life choices are based on my personal convictions. They aren't my recommendations for others who don't share those convictions.
M: Well, in this excerpt from your book, you argue that meat consumption and private transport are devastating the environment and that the best choices for the planet are vegetarian diets and public transport.
W: I did write that. But those are examples of what I call best practices, not what I'm actually suggesting. In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week.
M: You also endorse high taxes on meat and other animal products and increased taxes on gasoline. Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
W: But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only. Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: With me in the studio today is Ms. Jane Logan, author of a new book, Secrets to Success. She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. So Ms. Logan, in your book, you claim that successful people have many things in common. For instance, they know their strengths when pursuing a goal.
W: That's right. They also tend to be motivated by a negative or positive life event. They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them.
M: You also write that there are a number of different factors related to success. And while successful people are driven to achieve their goals, the ultra successful have even greater ambition.
W: Yes, greater ambition as well as a burning desire to be the best of the best is also a common characteristic.
M: Right. So those who are determined don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome.
W: Absolutely. Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals.
M: That's a good point. All too often, people give up at the first hurdle. Would you say then that most successful people make it all by themselves?
W: Not exactly. They are usually good at cooperating with people and understanding the needs of others.
M: So people will be willing to help them, I guess.
W: That's correct. And this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect, whether it's with a colleague, an assistant or even a receptionist.
M: Most successful people I know are very passionate about their work. Would you say that passion is the single biggest key to success?
W: Not entirely. There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion. If that exists, success will follow.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
The saying "blind as a bat" simply isn't correct. The truth is that all 1100 bat species can see and often their vision is pretty good, although not as excellent as other night-hunting animals.
There are two main groups of bats, which are believed to have evolved independently of each other, but both from a common ancestor. The first group, known as the mega bats, are mostly medium-sized or large bats who eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish. These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes. They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey. For example, Flying Foxes not only see well during daylight, but can also distinguish colors. They actually rely on their daylight vision and cannot fly during the night with no moonlight.
The second group, called micro bats, are smaller in size and mostly eat insects. These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food. Scientists have proven that despite their poorly developed small eyes, these bats still can see during the day. When we consider the nightly lifestyle of these bats, we will see they have to be sensitive to the changing light levels because this is how they sense when to start hunting. Moreover, vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances, beyond the range of echolocation.
So the truth is, there are no bats which are naturally blind. Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
A study has found that educational TV shows come with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior. Children who spend more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children. This shows that children can learn the educational lesson that was intended. However, they're also learning other things along the way.
This unintended impact has to do with the portrayal of conflict in media and how preschool-age children comprehend that conflict. TV and movie producers often incorporate an element of bad behavior. This is to teach children a lesson at the end of the program. Educational shows have pro-education and pro-social goals. However, conflict between characters is often depicted with characters being unkind to each other or they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other. Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story. That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together. You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that. These are still developing in young children.
However, parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing. Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot. Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end. They should explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate. This will help children interpret and get the message and help them learn to watch the show for those messages.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
While it has long been a practice in Asian countries, many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule. For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient. After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. But I can give you several good reasons why people should remove their shoes before going inside their homes.
Bacteria are everywhere. They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets. In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. And it only takes a little bit of dirt to damage your timber floors. The more dirt you track in, the more it scratches and the more often you'd have to clean. The extra scrubbing will harm your floors over time. Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels or shoes with pointed or hard parts. These can dent and scratch your floor. And if you live in an apartment building, removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors.
Walking around with bare feet is actually better for your feet. It strengthens the muscles in your feet. Though many people are accustomed to wearing shoes during all their waking hours, the more time you spend wearing shoes, the more likely you are to incur foot injuries as a result.
And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason. The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home. Toxic chemicals are everywhere in our lives: insect-killing chemicals used on public grass areas, cleaning chemicals on the floors of public areas. By kicking off your shoes before you enter the home, you are denying entry to these harmful chemicals.
Given the amount of time we spend in classrooms, and the number of shoes that pass through them every day, you may well understand me if I were to propose a no-shoes-in-the-classroom rule.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
Emotions are an essential and inseparable part of our consciousness. They are part of a built-in mechanism, which allows us to cope with the ups and downs of our lives both physically and mentally. When we hide our emotions and our true feelings, we stop being genuine, spontaneous and authentic in our relationships. When we put on cultivated and polished faces in the company of others, we stop being true to ourselves. Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust. Although humans are more advanced and intelligent, animals are more genuine and authentic in their behavior and responses than human beings. The more educated we are, the less transparent and reliable we become. We are drawn to our pets because pets do not lie.
One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human. There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional, unless your emotions make you inhuman, insensitive and cruel to others. Feelings of guilt associated with emotions are more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself. So when you deal with the problem of emotions, you should learn not only how to control them but also how to accept them and manage the guilt and anguish arising from them.
Our brains are made up of a primitive inner core and a more evolved and rational outer core. Most of the time, the rational part of the mind controls the information coming from the primitive core and makes its own decisions as to what to do and how to respond. However, during critical situations, especially when a threat is perceived, the outer core loses control and fails to regulate the impulses and instinctual responses coming from the primitive brain. As a result, we let disturbing thoughts and emotions arise in our consciousness and surrender to our primitive behavior.
In times of emotional turmoil, remember that emotions arise because your senses are wired to the primitive part of your mind which is self-regulated, autonomous and spontaneous. Your rational mind does not always deal with the messages coming from it effectively. These messages are part of your survival mechanism and should not be stifled simply because emotions are unhealthy and betray your weaknesses. When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. This way you make use of your emotions without losing your balance and inner stability.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Good morning, class. My topic today is how to feed a hungry world. The world's population is expected to grow from 6.8 billion today to 9.1 billion by 2050. Meanwhile, the world's population more than doubled from 3 billion between 1961 and 2007. Simultaneously, food production has been constrained by a lack of scientific research. Still, the task of feeding the world's population in 2050 seems easily possible.
What is needed is a second green revolution. This is an approach that is described as the sustainable growth of global agriculture. Such a revolution will require a wholesale shift of priorities in agricultural research. There is an urgent need for new crop varieties. They must offer higher yields but use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs. These new crops must also be more resistant to drought, heat and pests. Equally crucial is lower-tech research into basics such as crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms.
Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices. But that requires money. It is estimated that to meet the 2050 challenge, investment must double to 83 billion US dollars a year. Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure. Everything from production to storage and processing must improve. However, research agendas need to be focused on the needs of the poorest and most resource-limited countries. It is there that most of the world's population lives and it is there the population growth over the next decades will be the greatest.
To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view. In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations. But these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers.
The growth in public agricultural-research spending peaked in the 1970s and has been shrinking ever since. The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade. China seems set to transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries. But developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too. Calls by scientists for large increases in the appropriation of funds for public spending on agricultural research are more than justified.

questions.prompt: What do we learn about the woman's new book?
options: It has given rise to much controversy.
It has been very favorably received.
It was primarily written for vegetarians.
It offends many environmentalists.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about the woman's new book? 

 【翻译】 关于这位女士的新书我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它引起了很多争议。 
 B)  它受到了非常好的评价。 
 C)  它主要是为素食者写的。 
 D)  它冒犯了许多环保人士。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It has given rise to much controversy. 
 【定位】 P1 With me today is Meghan Brown, an environmental activist whose controversial new book Beyond Recycling is making headlines. 
 今天和我在一起的是梅根·布朗，一位环保活动家，她那本充满争议的新书《超越回收》正成为头条。 

 【信号】 开场介绍即定性句 。主持人开场介绍嘉宾时用 controversial new book 直接给书定了性，开场点题句往往就是答案句，不必等转折。 

 【替换】 controversial new book ↔ It has given rise to much controversy. 形容词转名词化 

 【排除】 B) 与原文相反 It has been very favorably received. 说广受好评，与原文 controversial(有争议)方向相反；有争议恰恰意味着评价两极，不等于一致叫好。  借用原文：controversial new book 

 C) 原词陷阱 It was primarily written for vegetarians. 借了后文反复出现的素食话题，但录音从未说这本书「主要写给素食者」；vegetarian 是真听到的词，可这句话原文没说，是典型听到原词就想选。  借用原文：They know I'm a vegetarian 

 D) 原词陷阱 It offends many environmentalists. 用了 environmentalist 这个反复出现的词，但原文说她被人「描绘成」环保活动家，从没说这本书「冒犯了许多环保人士」，属凭原词臆造。  借用原文：as a radical animal rights activist and environmentalist
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about the woman's new book?

questions.prompt: What do some critics say about the author of the book?
options: She neglects people's efforts in animal protection.
She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas.
She ignores the various benefits of public transport.
She insists vegetarians are harming the environment.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do some critics say about the author of the book? 

 【翻译】 一些批评者对这本书的作者有何评价? 
 A)  她忽视了人们在动物保护方面的努力。 
 B)  她试图强迫人们接受她的激进观点。 
 C)  她忽视了公共交通的各种好处。 
 D)  她坚持认为素食者正在危害环境。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas. 
 【定位】 P3 Critics of your book assert that you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country. Some claim that you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet and make private transport illegal. 
 你这本书的批评者断言，你想把激进的改变强加给整个国家。有人声称你想强迫所有人吃素食、把私人交通工具变成非法。 

 【信号】 Critics assert 转述信号 。出现 Critics of your book assert that 这一转述信号，明确告诉你下面就是批评者的说法，正对题干的 critics，是答案句标志。 

 【替换】 you're trying to force radical changes on the entire country ↔ She tries to force people to accept her radical ideas. 几近同词的核心保留 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 She neglects people's efforts in animal protection. 提到 animal protection 蹭了动物话题，但批评者从没说她「忽视他人的动保努力」，原文无此评价。 
 C) 原词陷阱 She ignores the various benefits of public transport. 用了反复出现的 public transport，但批评者根本没说她「无视公共交通的好处」——恰恰相反，她是支持公共交通的，这是把话题词乱拼成的指控。  借用原文：make private transport illegal 

 D) 张冠李戴 She insists vegetarians are harming the environment. 用了 vegetarian 和 environment 两个高频词，但批评者说的是她想强迫大家吃素，绝非说「素食者在破坏环境」，意思被拧反了。  借用原文：you want to force everyone to eat a vegetarian diet
questions.spoken_text: What do some critics say about the author of the book?

questions.prompt: What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested?
options: They are significant.
They are revolutionary.
They are rational.
They are modest.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested? 

 【翻译】 这位女士对她建议的饮食改变有何主张? 
 A)  它们是重大的。 
 B)  它们是革命性的。 
 C)  它们是合理的。 
 D)  它们是适度的。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They are modest. 
 【定位】 P8 In my guidelines for saving the environment, I suggest modest changes, like eating vegetarian meals two days a week. 
 在我那份保护环境的指南里，我建议的是温和的改变，比如每周吃两天素食。 

 【信号】 I suggest+定性词 。她亲口说 I suggest modest changes，suggest 后紧跟的形容词就是她对所建议改变的定性，是这题答案信号。 

 【替换】 I suggest modest changes ↔ They are modest. 同词直接还原 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 They are significant. 说重大，与她自述的 modest(温和)程度相反；她特意强调改变不大，significant 正好拧反。  借用原文：I suggest modest changes 

 B) 张冠李戴 They are revolutionary. 革命性，呼应了前文批评者说的 radical，但那是批评者的指控，她本人恰恰否认并改称 modest，把批评口吻当成她的定性就上当了。  借用原文：force radical changes 

 C) 未提及 They are rational. 理性的，听起来像褒义合理，但录音里她用的词是 modest 而非 rational，原文从未称这些改变「理性」。
questions.spoken_text: What does the woman claim about the diet changes she suggested?

questions.prompt: What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase?
options: It would help to protect the environment.
It would generate money for public health.
It would need support from the general public.
It would force poor people to change their diet.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase? 

 【翻译】 这位女士对她建议的增税有何看法? 
 A)  它将有助于保护环境。 
 B)  它将为公共卫生筹集资金。 
 C)  它需要公众的支持。 
 D)  它会迫使穷人改变他们的饮食。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） It would help to protect the environment. 
 【定位】 P10 But the taxes I suggest aren't that high, less than 3% only. Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection, which benefits everyone. 
 但我建议的税率没那么高，只有不到3%。而且，所产生的钱会被用于环境保护，这对每个人都有益。 

 【信号】 Plus 之后补出关键好处 。她先用 But 澄清税不高，再用 Plus, the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection 补出加税的去向与好处，Plus 引出的这句才是她想强调的作用，是答案句。 

 【替换】 the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection ↔ It would help to protect the environment. 措施钱去向=保护环境 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 It would generate money for public health. 借了原文 the money generated，但钱的去向是 environmental protection(环保)而非 public health(公共卫生)，把用途偷换了。  借用原文：the money generated would be allocated to environmental protection 

 C) 未提及 It would need support from the general public. 听着合理，但她谈加税时只说税率低、钱用于环保，从没说这措施「需要公众支持」，是无中生有。 
 D) 张冠李戴 It would force poor people to change their diet. 含 force 和 poor people，但这是主持人质疑时的说法(第9段)，正是她要反驳的，不是她自己对加税的说法，题干问的是她怎么说。  借用原文：Those taxes could force poor people to adopt your life choices.
questions.spoken_text: What does the woman say about her suggested tax increase?

questions.prompt: What has the woman revealed in her book?
options: Where successful people's strengths come from.
Why many people fight so hard for success.
How she achieved her life's goal.
What makes people successful.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the woman revealed in her book? 

 【翻译】 这位女士在她的书中揭示了什么? 
 A)  成功人士的优势来自哪里。 
 B)  为什么许多人如此努力地追求成功。 
 C)  她如何实现了自己的人生目标。 
 D)  是什么使人们成功。 

 【答案】 D （主旨题） What makes people successful. 
 【定位】 P1 She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. 
 她声称揭示了人们是如何获得成功的。 

 【信号】 开头点题句 。主持人开场介绍时一句 She claims to have uncovered how people achieve success. 直接交代了全书主题，开头点题正是主旨题的核心定位信号。 

 【替换】 how people achieve success ↔ What makes people successful. "如何获得成功"="什么造就成功" 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确说成功者 they know their strengths when pursuing a goal，A 把 strengths 单拎出来问 "strengths 从哪来"，但 "strengths 的来源" 录音根本没讲，且它只是众多特征之一，不是全书主旨。  借用原文：they know their strengths when pursuing a goal 

 B) 未提及 B 问 "为什么很多人拼命追求成功"（原因），但全篇谈的是成功者 "有哪些共同特征"，从未讨论 "人为何要拼命求成功" 这个动机问题，属无中生有。 
 C) 张冠李戴 C 说 "她（作者）如何实现人生目标"，但录音里这位女士是在 "揭示别人成功的规律"，谈的是 people / successful people，不是讲她自己的成功经历，主语张冠李戴。

questions.prompt: What do successful people attribute their achievements to?
options: Having someone who has confidence in them.
Having someone who is ready to help them.
Having a firm belief in their own ability.
Having a realistic attitude towards life.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do successful people attribute their achievements to? 

 【翻译】 成功人士将他们的成就归功于什么? 
 A)  有一个对他们有信心的人。 
 B)  有一个随时准备帮助他们的人。 
 C)  对自己的能力有坚定的信念。 
 D)  对生活有现实的态度。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Having someone who has confidence in them. 
 【定位】 P2 They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them. 
 他们把成功归功于生命中有一个相信他们的人。 

 【信号】 归因信号 credit...to 。被问者（女士）的应答 They credit their success to having someone in their life who believes in them. 中 credit...to（归功于）正是归因信号，它后面跟的就是答案点。 

 【替换】 someone in their life who believes in them ↔ Having someone who has confidence in them. believes in=has confidence in 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B "有人随时愿帮他们" 与 A 仅差核心词。录音说的是 someone who believes in them（相信），不是 "愿意帮忙"。"愿帮忙" 是后文 people will be willing to help them 才提到、且属另一道题的内容，搬到这里就答非所问。  借用原文：people will be willing to help them 

 C) 偷换概念 C "对自身能力有坚定信念" 把主语换成了 "自己"，而录音明确是 someone...who believes in them——是 "别人相信他"，主语方向相反。 
 D) 未提及 D "对生活持现实态度" 在整段归因表述里完全没出现，录音只说归功于 "有人相信他们"，与 "现实态度" 无关，属无中生有。
questions.spoken_text: What do successful people attribute their achievements to?

questions.prompt: What do successful people do when faced with difficulties?
options: They adjust their goals accordingly.
They try hard to appear optimistic.
They stay positive.
They remain calm.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do successful people do when faced with difficulties? 

 【翻译】 成功人士在面对困难时会做什么? 
 A)  他们相应地调整自己的目标。 
 B)  他们努力表现出乐观的样子。 
 C)  他们保持积极。 
 D)  他们保持冷静。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They stay positive. 
 【定位】 P6 Successful people are also optimistic as it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles that can deter us from achieving our goals. 
 成功者也很乐观，因为在意识到那些会阻碍我们达成目标的障碍的同时，保持积极是很重要的。 

 【信号】 困难词 obstacles 附近的描述 。被问者说 it is important to stay positive while being aware of obstacles，obstacles（障碍）这一困难词附近，紧跟的 stay positive 正是成功者面对困难的反应。 

 【替换】 stay positive ↔ They stay positive. 原话直接对应 
 Successful people are also optimistic ↔ stay positive optimistic 与 positive 同义 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A "相应调整目标"，但录音第 5 段说成功者 don't see obstacles as something that prevents success, but mere inconveniences that need to be overcome——是 "克服障碍" 而非 "改目标"，方向相反。  借用原文：mere inconveniences that need to be overcome 

 B) 偷换概念 B "努力让自己显得乐观"，录音确说 optimistic、stay positive，但那是 "真的保持积极"，不是 "appear（装作）乐观"，selflessly 加了一个 "装样子" 的意思，曲解原意。  借用原文：Successful people are also optimistic 

 D) 偷换概念 D "remain calm（保持冷静）" 与 C "stay positive（保持积极）" 极易混，但录音说的是 positive / optimistic（积极乐观），从未说 calm（冷静），用近义词偷梁换柱。

questions.prompt: What is one prerequisite for passion at work according to the woman?
options: An understanding leadership.
A nurturing environment.
Mutual respect among colleagues.
Highly cooperative teammates.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is one prerequisite for passion at work according to the woman? 

 【翻译】 根据这位女士的说法,工作中拥有热情的一个先决条件是什么? 
 A)  善解人意的领导。 
 B)  培育性的环境。 
 C)  同事之间的相互尊重。 
 D)  高度合作的团队成员。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） A nurturing environment. 
 【定位】 P12 There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion. 
 有一个前提条件，那就是，你必须在一个能培育激情的环境里工作。 

 【信号】 明示信号 prerequisite + have to 。被问者直接说 There's a prerequisite, that is, you have to work in an environment that nurtures passion.，prerequisite（前提）加 have to（必须）双重 "必需" 信号，答案点就在其后。 

 【替换】 an environment that nurtures passion ↔ A nurturing environment. 动词短语压缩成名词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A "an understanding leadership"，前提句只讲 "培育激情的环境"，全程未提 "领导"；understanding 一词倒是在别处 understanding the needs of others 出现过、但那是讲 "理解他人需求" 的合作，与领导无关。  借用原文：understanding the needs of others 

 C) 原词陷阱 C "同事间相互尊重"，mutual respect 确在录音 this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect 出现过，但那是讲合作 "带来" 的结果、且属第 6-7 题语境，不是 "激情的前提"，搬来此处答非所问。  借用原文：this often leads to a great deal of mutual respect 

 D) 张冠李戴 D "highly cooperative teammates"，录音确说成功者 good at cooperating with people，但那是讲成功者自身的合作能力，不是 "激情的前提"；把合作内容嫁接到前提题上属张冠李戴。  借用原文：good at cooperating with people

questions.prompt: What do we learn about mega bats?
options: They use their sense of hearing to capture their prey.
Their food mainly consists of small animals and fish.
They have big eyes and distinctive visual centers.
Their ancestor is different from that of micro bats.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about mega bats? 

 【翻译】 关于大型蝙蝠我们了解到什么？ 
 A)  它们使用听觉捕捉猎物。 
 B)  它们的食物主要由小型动物和鱼类组成。 
 C)  它们有大眼睛和独特的视觉中枢。 
 D)  它们的祖先与小型蝙蝠的祖先不同。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They have big eyes and distinctive visual centers. 
 【定位】 P2 These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes. 
 这些物种拥有发达独特的视觉中枢和大眼睛。 

 【信号】 对象+特征的直陈句 。录音在介绍 mega bats 后紧接一句专讲其生理特征 These species have distinctive visual centers and big eyes.，这种紧贴对象的直陈描述句就是承载特征题答案的句子。 

 【替换】 distinctive visual centers and big eyes ↔ big eyes and distinctive visual centers 同内容换语序 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 录音说 mega bats 是 They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.，靠视觉和嗅觉捕食；A 把别处提到的 sense of hearing 安到 mega bats 头上，且 mega 用的根本不是听觉。  借用原文：They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey. 

 B) 原词陷阱 录音确实念到 eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish，B 盗用了 small animals and fish 这几个原词，但只截取了一部分（漏了 fruits, flowers）、把偶尔吃说成主食，是以偏概全的原词陷阱。  借用原文：eat fruits, flowers, and sometimes small animals or fish 

 D) 与原文相反 录音说两类蝙蝠 both from a common ancestor，是共同祖先；D 称 mega 的祖先与 micro 不同，正好与原文相反，是把同变成了不同。  借用原文：both from a common ancestor
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn about mega bats?

questions.prompt: How do micro bats find their way and identify food?
options: With the help of moonlight.
By means of echolocation.
With the aid of daylight vision.
By means of vision and smell.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How do micro bats find their way and identify food? 

 【翻译】 小型蝙蝠如何找到方向并识别食物？ 
 A)  借助月光。 
 B)  通过回声定位。 
 C)  借助日光视觉。 
 D)  通过视觉和嗅觉。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） By means of echolocation. 
 【定位】 P3 These species use echolocation to find their way and identify food. 
 这些物种利用回声定位来找路和辨别食物。 

 【信号】 方式动词use直陈手段 。录音用 use echolocation to find their way and identify food 把手段（echolocation）和目的（find way / identify food）一句说全，use 后接的就是 How 题要的方式，是标准答案句。 

 【替换】 use echolocation ↔ By means of echolocation 动词改介词短语 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音 moonlight 出现在讲 mega bats 的 cannot fly during the night with no moonlight，是说没月光就飞不了，既不是 micro bats、又是个否定语境；A 盗 moonlight 这个原词答非所问。  借用原文：cannot fly during the night with no moonlight 

 C) 张冠李戴 daylight vision 是录音描述 mega bats（Flying Foxes）的 rely on their daylight vision，C 把 mega 的本领安到 micro bats 的找路方式上，张冠李戴。  借用原文：rely on their daylight vision 

 D) 张冠李戴 vision and smell 出自 mega bats 的 They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.，是 mega 的捕食手段；D 把这套手段挪给 micro bats 找路，盗原词又张冠李戴。  借用原文：They use senses of vision and smell to capture their prey.
questions.spoken_text: How do microbats find their way and identify food?

questions.prompt: Why do some species of bats use their sense of hearing more than their eyes?
options: To make up for their natural absence of vision.
To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle.
To facilitate their travel over long distances.
To survive in the ever-changing weather.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why do some species of bats use their sense of hearing more than their eyes? 

 【翻译】 为什么某些种类的蝙蝠使用听觉多于使用眼睛？ 
 A)  为了弥补它们天生缺乏视觉。 
 B)  为了适应特定的生活方式。 
 C)  为了便于长距离飞行。 
 D)  为了在不断变化的天气中生存。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle. 
 【定位】 P4 Some species use their sense of hearing more than their eyes as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle, but their eyes are still functional. 
 有些物种更多地依赖听觉而非眼睛，这是对某种特定生活方式的一种适应，但它们的眼睛依然是有功能的。 

 【信号】 as a matter of点出原因 。末段用 as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle 直接给出更依赖听觉的缘由，as a matter of 是显式的原因信号，这句就是 Why 题的答案句。 

 【替换】 as a matter of adaptation to a particular lifestyle ↔ To adapt themselves to a particular lifestyle 名词化改不定式 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 录音末段明确 there are no bats which are naturally blind、眼睛仍 functional；A 称要弥补天生没视力，与原文 naturally blind 的否定恰好相反。  借用原文：there are no bats which are naturally blind 

 C) 原词陷阱 long distances 出自第三段 vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances，说的是视觉的用途；C 盗这个原词来回答更依赖听觉的原因，答非所问。  借用原文：vision is used by micro bats to travel over long distances 

 D) 未提及 录音从未把更依赖听觉归因于应对天气，weather 一词全篇没出现；D 是凭空添加的原因，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: Why do some species of bats use their sense of hearing more than their eyes?

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about children watching educational programs?
options: They acquire knowledge not found in books.
They learn how to interact with their peers.
They become more emotionally aggressive.
They get much better prepared for school.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about children watching educational programs? 

 【翻译】 文章关于儿童观看教育节目说了什么？ 
 A)  他们获得了书本上找不到的知识。 
 B)  他们学会了如何与同龄人互动。 
 C)  他们在情感上变得更具攻击性。 
 D)  他们为上学做了更充分的准备。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They become more emotionally aggressive. 
 【定位】 P1 Children who spend more time watching educational programs increase their emotional aggression toward other children. 
 花更多时间看教育类节目的孩子，会增加他们对其他孩子的情绪攻击性。 

 【信号】 话题词定位 + 反预期的负面定性 。录音开头说研究发现教育节目"comes with an added lesson that influences the child's behavior"，随即点出 increase their emotional aggression toward other children——这个"与直觉相反的负面结果"正是研究要讲的核心，是答案句的信号。 

 【替换】 increase their emotional aggression toward other children ↔ become more emotionally aggressive 动宾结构改写为系表结构 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音确实反复说 educational、added lesson，They acquire knowledge not found in books. 顺势编出"学到书本外的知识"，但 learn the educational lesson that was intended 说的是"学到了节目本意要教的内容"，并非"书本里没有的知识"，属听到 lesson 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：learn the educational lesson that was intended 

 B) 未提及 They learn how to interact with their peers."学会与同伴相处"听起来很像教育节目的好处，但录音通篇讲的是孩子对其他孩子"increase emotional aggression"，恰恰是相处变差，从未说学会良性互动，属未提及。 
 D) 过度推断 They get much better prepared for school. 与录音 learn to watch the show for those messages 的方向无关，录音从没说看节目让孩子"更适应学校"；它借"教育"联想到"上学"，是凭常识推过头的正向结论。
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say about children watching educational programs?

questions.prompt: Why can't preschool children get the moral conveyed in the TV programs?
options: They are far from emotionally prepared.
They tend to be more attracted by images.
They can't follow the conflicts in the show.
They lack the cognitive and memory skills.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why can't preschool children get the moral conveyed in the TV programs? 

 【翻译】 为什么学龄前儿童无法理解电视节目中传达的道德寓意？ 
 A)  他们在情感上还远未做好准备。 
 B)  他们往往更容易被画面吸引。 
 C)  他们无法理解节目中的冲突。 
 D)  他们缺乏认知和记忆技能。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They lack the cognitive and memory skills. 
 【定位】 P2 That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together. You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills to be able to do that. These are still developing in young children. 
 那是因为这要求他们理解节目所有部分如何拼接在一起。要做到这点，你需要相当复杂的认知能力和记忆能力。而这些能力在幼儿身上还在发育之中。 

 【信号】 因果信号 That's because 直接领出原因 。录音先说 Preschool children really don't get the moral of the story，紧接 That's because it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together——That's because 是明确的因果信号，其后两句给出真正原因：需要复杂的认知与记忆能力，而幼儿这些能力还在发育。 

 【替换】 You need pretty complicated cognitive skills and memory skills ↔ They lack the cognitive and memory skills. "需要却还在发育"="缺乏"的肯否定转换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音里 emotional 多次出现（emotional aggression、emotionally aggressive tactics），They are far from emotionally prepared. 借这个 emotionally 编出"情绪上远未准备好"，但录音解释孩子领会不了寓意，归因的是认知记忆能力，而非情绪准备，属听到 emotionally 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：they may use emotionally aggressive tactics with each other 

 B) 未提及 They tend to be more attracted by images."更易被画面吸引"是关于幼儿看电视的常识印象，但录音解释"领会不了寓意"时根本没提画面或图像，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 录音确有 the portrayal of conflict in media 与角色间冲突的描述，They can't follow the conflicts in the show. 借 conflict 编出"跟不上剧中冲突"；但录音说孩子缺的是把"all the parts fit together"整体串联的能力，不是单看不懂冲突这一点，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：it requires that they understand how all the parts of the show fit together
questions.spoken_text: Why can't preschool children get the moral conveyed in the TV programs?

questions.prompt: What does the passage suggest parents do?
options: Choose appropriate programs for their children.
Help their children understand the program's plot.
Outline the program's plot for their children first.
Monitor their children's watching of TV programs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage suggest parents do? 

 【翻译】 文章建议家长做什么？ 
 A)  为孩子选择合适的节目。 
 B)  帮助孩子理解节目的情节。 
 C)  先为孩子概述节目的情节。 
 D)  监督孩子观看电视节目。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Help their children understand the program's plot. 
 【定位】 P3 Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot. 
 父母反而应该和孩子一起看，并帮助他们理解剧情。 

 【信号】 建议信号 should + 转折 instead 。录音先说 parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing（不该完全限制孩子观看），紧接 Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot——should 加 instead 的组合，正是"否定旧做法、给出新建议"的强信号，instead 后才是真正建议。 

 【替换】 help them to understand the plot ↔ Help their children understand the program's plot. 代词还原 + 几乎同义复述 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 录音 program/programs 多次出现，Choose appropriate programs for their children. 借此编出"为孩子挑合适的节目"，但录音的建议是陪看并帮孩子理解，从没说"挑选节目"，属听到 programs 就想选的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Parents should instead watch with their kids and help them to understand the plot 

 C) 原词陷阱 Outline the program's plot for their children first. 借录音里的 plot 编出"先给孩子概述情节"，但录音说的是"帮孩子理解情节（help them understand the plot）"，是陪着理解，而非父母先单方面 outline，属原词陷阱加偷换概念。  借用原文：help them to understand the plot 

 D) 与原文相反 Monitor their children's watching of TV programs."监督孩子看电视"听着像合理建议，但录音明说 parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing——反对单纯管控，主张陪看引导。D 取的恰是录音否定掉的方向，属与原文相反。  借用原文：parents shouldn't completely constrain children's viewing
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage suggest parents do?

questions.prompt: What should parents do right after watching the TV program?
options: Explain its message to their children.
Check if their children have enjoyed it.
Encourage their children to retell the story.
Ask their children to describe its characters.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should parents do right after watching the TV program? 

 【翻译】 家长在观看完电视节目后应该立即做什么？ 
 A)  向孩子解释节目的寓意。 
 B)  检查孩子是否喜欢这个节目。 
 C)  鼓励孩子复述故事。 
 D)  让孩子描述节目中的人物。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Explain its message to their children. 
 【定位】 P3 Parents can comment along the way and then explain the message at the end. 
 父母可以在观看过程中随时点评，然后在结尾时解释其寓意。 

 【信号】 时间对照 along the way 对 at the end 。录音把父母的动作按时间分两段：comment along the way（看的过程中点评）与 explain the message at the end（在结尾解释寓意）。题干问的是 right after（看完之后），对应的正是 at the end 这一时点的动作，时间标志 at the end 是定位信号。 

 【替换】 explain the message at the end ↔ Explain its message to their children. 时间状语换补语，动宾近乎照搬 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 Check if their children have enjoyed it."看孩子是否喜欢"是看完节目后家长常做的常识动作，但录音讲看完后是"explain the message（解释寓意）"，从未提"问喜不喜欢"，属未提及。 
 C) 偷换概念 Encourage their children to retell the story. 与录音相近的是"看完后做点什么"，但录音的动作是父母"explain the message（解释寓意）"，是父母讲给孩子，不是"鼓励孩子复述"，主语和动作都被偷换，属偷换概念。  借用原文：explain the message at the end 

 D) 原词陷阱 录音结尾说父母要 explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate（解释某些行为为何不当），Ask their children to describe its characters. 借"行为/角色"的联想编出"让孩子描述角色"，但录音是父母讲解行为是否得当，不是让孩子描述人物，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：explain how certain types of behavior were not appropriate
questions.spoken_text: What should parents do right after watching the TV program?

questions.prompt: Why don't many Westerners take off shoes before entering a house?
options: They are afraid of injuring their feet.
They have never developed the habit.
They believe a little dirt harms no one.
They find it rather troublesome to do so.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why don't many Westerners take off shoes before entering a house? 

 【翻译】 为什么许多西方人在进屋前不脱鞋? 
 A)  他们担心伤到自己的脚。 
 B)  他们从未养成这个习惯。 
 C)  他们认为一点脏东西不会伤害任何人。 
 D)  他们觉得这样做相当麻烦。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They believe a little dirt harms no one. 
 【定位】 P1 For many in those countries, wiping their shoes before going inside is regarded as sufficient. After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. 
 对那些国家的许多人来说，进门前把鞋蹭一蹭就算够了。毕竟，他们也许觉得一点脏东西伤不了谁。 

 【信号】 After all 引出真实想法 。答案落在 After all, they may think a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone. 这句，信号词是 After all——它引出 "人们之所以不脱鞋" 背后的真实想法，是这道原因题的落点。 

 【替换】 a little dirt doesn't hurt anyone ↔ a little dirt harms no one 同义改写：hurt anyone = harm no one 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They are afraid of injuring their feet. 盗用了原文 incur foot injuries 这个 "脚受伤" 的字眼，但原文那句是说 "穿鞋越久越容易伤脚"，是赤脚有益的论据，根本不是 "西方人不脱鞋的原因"，属听到 "伤脚" 就误选。  借用原文：the more likely you are to incur foot injuries 

 B) They have never developed the habit. 听上去合理，但原文只说脱鞋 has long been a practice in Asian countries、西方人 have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule，是在陈述 "做不做" 的现状，从未把 "没养成习惯" 点为他们不脱鞋的原因，属原文未明说的推断。  借用原文：many people in Western countries have yet to embrace the no-shoes-in-the-house rule 

 D) They find it rather troublesome to do so. 在原文里找不到对应——说话人只说他们觉得蹭蹭鞋 is regarded as sufficient（就够了），从没说他们 "嫌脱鞋麻烦"，这是凭生活常识脑补出来的，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: Why don't many Westerners take off shoes before entering a house?

questions.prompt: What is the finding of one study by researchers at an American university?
options: Different types of bacteria existed on public-toilet floors.
There were more bacteria on sidewalks than in the home.
Office carpets collected more bacteria than elsewhere.
A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the finding of one study by researchers at an American university? 

 【翻译】 美国一所大学的研究人员进行的一项研究有什么发现? 
 A)  公共厕所地板上存在不同类型的细菌。 
 B)  人行道上的细菌比家中的多。 
 C)  办公室地毯比其他地方收集的细菌更多。 
 D)  单只鞋子上收集了大量细菌。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe. 
 【定位】 P2 In one study conducted at an American university, researchers collected microscopic germs from footwear. They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe. 
 在美国一所大学开展的一项研究中，研究人员从鞋上采集了微观细菌。他们发现，一只鞋的外侧最多可聚集多达 42.1 万个单位的细菌。 

 【信号】 They found 引出研究结论 。信号是 In one study conducted at an American university 点出研究，紧接 They found that up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe 用 "They found" 抛出具体发现——一只鞋上多达 42.1 万单位细菌，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 up to 421,000 units of bacteria can collect on the outside of a single shoe ↔ A large number of bacteria collected on a single shoe 具体数字概括为 a large number 

 【排除】 A) Different types of bacteria existed on public-toilet floors. 盗用原文 public toilet floors 这个原词，但那句 They collect on your shoes when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets 是泛说 "细菌哪里都有"，并非那项研究的发现；且 "不同种类的细菌" 原文也没提，属张冠李戴加无中生有。  借用原文：public toilet floors 

 B) There were more bacteria on sidewalks than in the home. 盗用 sidewalks 一词，但原文只把人行道与公厕、办公室地毯并列说 "都会沾菌"，从没拿 "人行道" 和 "家中" 作 more…than 的比较，这个比较是凭空加上去的。  借用原文：when you walk along sidewalks, public toilet floors and even office carpets 

 C) Office carpets collected more bacteria than elsewhere. 盗用原文 office carpets，但原文只把办公室地毯当作 "也会沾菌" 的并列地点之一，还用 even 表示 "连地毯都沾"，绝没有说它 "比别处收集得多"，属偷换为最高级/比较级。  借用原文：and even office carpets

questions.prompt: What is the final reason the speaker gives for removing shoes before entering a house?
options: The chemicals on shoes can deteriorate air quality.
Shoes can upset family members with their noise.
The marks left by shoes are hard to erase.
Shoes can leave scratches on the floor.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the final reason the speaker gives for removing shoes before entering a house? 

 【翻译】 说话者给出的进屋前脱鞋的最后一个理由是什么? 
 A)  鞋子上的化学物质会使空气质量恶化。 
 B)  鞋子的噪音会打扰家庭成员。 
 C)  鞋子留下的痕迹很难清除。 
 D)  鞋子会在地板上留下划痕。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） The chemicals on shoes can deteriorate air quality. 
 【定位】 P4 And if people aren't yet convinced by my arguments, I can give one final reason. The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home. 
 如果有人还没被我的论据说服，我可以再给出最后一个理由。你通过鞋子带进家里的灰尘和有毒化学物质，会让家中的空气质量变差。 

 【信号】 one final reason 标志收尾理由 。信号是 I can give one final reason——"one final reason" 明确宣告这是最后一个理由，紧跟其后的 The dust and toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality in your home 即答案句。 

 【替换】 toxic chemicals you bring into your house via your shoes can deteriorate the air quality ↔ The chemicals on shoes can deteriorate air quality 几乎同义、deteriorate 原样保留 

 【排除】 B) Shoes can upset family members with their noise. 盗用第 2 段 removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do 里的 "noisy/噪音" 概念，但原文那是说为楼下邻居着想，针对的是 downstairs neighbors 而非 family members，且它出现在中间、不是 "最后一个" 理由，属张冠李戴加位置错位。  借用原文：removing your noisy shoes is the polite thing to do out of consideration for your downstairs neighbors 

 C) 未提及 The marks left by shoes are hard to erase. 盗用第 2 段 leave marks and scratches on floors 的 "marks"，但原文只说鞋会留下痕迹划痕、会损伤地板，从没说这些痕迹 "难以清除"，"hard to erase" 是脑补；而且这属第 2 段的地板理由，不是最后理由。  借用原文：Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors 

 D) Shoes can leave scratches on the floor. 几乎照搬第 2 段原词 leave marks and scratches on floors，内容原文确实说了，但它是中间列举的地板理由之一，不是题目要的 "one final reason"，属答非所问的原词陷阱。  借用原文：Shoes can also leave marks and scratches on floors, especially high heels

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say about hiding one's emotions?
options: It is sinful and immoral.
It is deemed uncivilized.
It is an uncontrollable behavior.
It is a violation of faith and trust.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say about hiding one's emotions? 

 【翻译】 说话者关于隐藏情绪说了什么? 
 A)  这是有罪的和不道德的。 
 B)  这被认为是不文明的。 
 C)  这是一种无法控制的行为。 
 D)  这是对信念和信任的违背。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） It is a violation of faith and trust. 
 【定位】 P1 Socially, it may be a good tactic to hide our true emotions, but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust. 
 在社交上，隐藏真实情绪也许是个不错的策略，但在道德上，它也是一种对信任的背弃。 

 【信号】 转折 but + morally 后才是真意 。前半 Socially, it may be a good tactic 是退一步的让步，真正的定性在 but morally it is also a breach of faith and trust，转折词 but 与立场状语 morally 之后那句才是说话人的态度落点。 

 【替换】 a breach of faith and trust ↔ a violation of faith and trust breach = violation 近义替换 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 It is sinful and immoral. 借用了第二段 There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional 里的原词，但那是在说"有情绪本身"并不可耻，且原文用的是 nothing... 的否定，与"隐藏情绪"无关。  借用原文：There is nothing sinful or immoral about being emotional 

 B) 未提及 It is deemed uncivilized. 说"被视为不文明"，但录音通篇没把隐藏情绪定性为"不文明"，属凭常识臆测的无中生有。 
 C) 张冠李戴 It is an uncontrollable behavior. 的"控制"主题来自第二、三段讲情绪如何被理性脑调控，与"隐藏情绪是何性质"无关，且原文从未说隐藏情绪"无法控制"。  借用原文：the rational part of the mind controls the information

questions.prompt: What should we do first in dealing with emotions?
options: Assess their consequences.
Guard against their harm.
Accept them as normal.
Find out their causes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should we do first in dealing with emotions? 

 【翻译】 在处理情绪时我们首先应该做什么? 
 A)  评估它们的后果。 
 B)  防范它们的危害。 
 C)  接受它们是正常的。 
 D)  找出它们的原因。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Accept them as normal. 
 【定位】 P2 One of the first steps in dealing with emotions such as anger or fear is to acknowledge them as normal and human. 
 处理愤怒或恐惧这类情绪的第一步，是承认它们是正常的、属于人之常情的。 

 【信号】 首步标志 one of the first steps 。One of the first steps in dealing with emotions 直接对应题干的 do first，是明确的首步信号，其后的 to acknowledge them as normal and human 就是要做的第一步动作。 

 【替换】 to acknowledge them as normal and human ↔ Accept them as normal. acknowledge≈accept、保留 as normal 

 【排除】 A) 答非所问 Assess their consequences. 中的"后果"虽与第二段 more devastating and damaging 的语气沾边，但原文从未把"评估后果"列为第一步，是借语气制造的答非所问。  借用原文：more devastating and damaging than the experience of emotion itself 

 B) 与原文相反 Guard against their harm. 主张"提防情绪的危害"，但本段恰恰说"有情绪没什么可耻"、要接纳，立场相反，并非要防备情绪。  借用原文：acknowledge them as normal and human 

 D) 未提及 Find out their causes. 说找出情绪的成因，录音里并未把"找原因"列为处理情绪的第一步，属凭常识联想的无中生有。

questions.prompt: What are we advised to do when emotions arise?
options: Try to understand what messages they convey.
Pay attention to their possible consequences.
Consider them from different perspectives.
Make sure they are brought under control.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What are we advised to do when emotions arise? 

 【翻译】 当情绪出现时,我们被建议做什么? 
 A)  试着理解它们传达了什么信息。 
 B)  注意它们可能产生的后果。 
 C)  从不同的角度考虑它们。 
 D)  确保它们得到控制。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Try to understand what messages they convey. 
 【定位】 P4 When emotions arise, instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver. 
 当情绪升起时，不要压抑它们，而要留意它们，并试着理解它们想要传达的信息。 

 【信号】 建议信号 instead of...pay attention to 。情境词 When emotions arise 与题干完全对应，紧跟的 instead of stifling them, pay attention to them and try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver 是明确建议句，instead of（而不是）排除了"压抑"、点出真正主张。 

 【替换】 try to understand the messages they are trying to deliver ↔ Try to understand what messages they convey. deliver=convey、句式微调 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Pay attention to their possible consequences. 用了 pay attention to（原文确有 pay attention to them），却把宾语偷换成 consequences —— 原文要留意的是情绪本身/其信息，不是后果。  借用原文：pay attention to them 

 C) 未提及 Consider them from different perspectives. 说"从不同角度看待"，录音末段并无"多角度"之说，属听起来不错但原文没有的无中生有。 
 D) 与原文相反 Make sure they are brought under control. 借了全文反复出现的 control，但末段恰恰主张 instead of stifling them —— 不要压制、而要倾听，方向正相反。  借用原文：instead of stifling them

questions.prompt: What is an urgent need for feeding the world's population in 2050, according to the speaker?
options: Cultivation of new varieties of crops.
Measures to cope with climate change.
Development of more effective pesticides.
Application of more nitrogen-rich fertilizers.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is an urgent need for feeding the world's population in 2050, according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者所说,到2050年养活世界人口的迫切需求是什么? 
 A)  培育新品种作物。 
 B)  应对气候变化的措施。 
 C)  开发更有效的杀虫剂。 
 D)  施用更多富氮肥料。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Cultivation of new varieties of crops. 
 【定位】 P2 There is an urgent need for new crop varieties. 
 迫切需要新的作物品种。 

 【信号】 urgent need 强调信号 。题干钩子词在第二段原句 There is an urgent need for new crop varieties 里几乎原样出现,urgent need 这一强调结构直接顶出了答案对象 new crop varieties,这就是答案句信号。 

 【替换】 new crop varieties ↔ Cultivation of new varieties of crops 同概念换序改写 

 【排除】 B) 过度推断 录音确实说新品种要 more resistant to drought, heat and pests(抗旱、抗热、抗虫),B 把"抗热"过度引申成 Measures to cope with climate change(应对气候变化),拔高了原文,录音并未把"应对气候变化"列为急需。  借用原文：more resistant to drought, heat and pests 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 的 pesticides(农药)是借录音 more resistant to ... pests 里的 pests(害虫)来诱选,但录音讲的是"新品种本身要抗虫",根本没提"研发更有效的农药",方向相反。  借用原文：more resistant to drought, heat and pests 

 D) 与原文相反 D 直接盗用录音原词 nitrogen-rich fertilizers,但录音说新品种要 use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs(少用水、少用氮肥),D 却说 Application of more nitrogen-rich fertilizers(施更多氮肥),把"少用"反成了"多用"。  借用原文：use less water, nitrogen-rich fertilizers or other inputs

questions.prompt: Where should most of the money be invested to feed the ever-growing population?
options: The expansion of farmland in developing countries.
The research on crop rotation in developing countries.
The cooperation of the world's agricultural scientists.
The improvement of agricultural infrastructure.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Where should most of the money be invested to feed the ever-growing population? 

 【翻译】 为了养活不断增长的人口,大部分资金应该投资在哪里? 
 A)  发展中国家的农田扩张。 
 B)  发展中国家的轮作研究。 
 C)  世界各国农业科学家的合作。 
 D)  农业基础设施的改善。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The improvement of agricultural infrastructure. 
 【定位】 P3 Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure. 
 那笔钱的大部分需要用于改善农业基础设施。 

 【信号】 Most of money go towards 直陈投向 。第三段原句 Most of that money needs to go towards improving agricultural infrastructure 与题干 most of the money 措辞对应,go towards 直接交代了钱的去向,是答案句的明确信号。 

 【替换】 improving agricultural infrastructure ↔ The improvement of agricultural infrastructure 动词名词化改写 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 借 Developing nations 这个原词造"发展中国家"的熟悉感,但录音讲的是发展中国家"更好地运用现代技术"来增产,从未提 expansion of farmland(扩大耕地),属无中生有。  借用原文：Developing nations could score substantial gains in productivity by making better use of modern technologies and practices 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 的 crop rotation 盗自第二段 crop rotation and mixed farming,那是讲"需要低技术研究的基础项",和本题"钱投在哪"无关;B 把跨段细节硬拼成投资对象,答非所问。  借用原文：crop rotation and mixed farming of animals and plants on small farms 

 C) 张冠李戴 C 的 cooperation of the world's agricultural scientists 来自第四段 the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view 一带的内容,讲的是科学家联手开会,与本题"钱主要投哪"是两码事,张冠李戴。  借用原文：the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view

questions.prompt: Why does the speaker give credit to the world's agricultural scientists?
options: For encouraging farmers to embrace new farming techniques.
For aligning their research with advances in farming technology.
For turning their focus to the needs of farmers in poorer countries.
For cooperating closely with policymakers in developing countries.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the speaker give credit to the world's agricultural scientists? 

 【翻译】 说话者为什么称赞世界各国的农业科学家? 
 A)  因为鼓励农民接受新的耕作技术。 
 B)  因为使他们的研究与农业技术进步保持一致。 
 C)  因为将他们的重点转向较贫穷国家农民的需求。 
 D)  因为与发展中国家的政策制定者密切合作。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） For turning their focus to the needs of farmers in poorer countries. 
 【定位】 P4 To their credit, the world's agricultural scientists are embracing such a broad view. In March, for example, they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research to begin working out how to change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations. 
 值得称道的是,全球农业科学家们正在接受这样一种宽阔的视野。比如今年三月,他们齐聚首届全球农业研究大会,着手研究如何调整研究议程,以帮助满足较贫困国家农民的需求。 

 【信号】 To their credit 表扬信号引出原因 。第四段以 To their credit(值得称道的是)这一肯定信号开头,紧跟 came together at the first Global Conference(齐聚大会)交代了被表扬的具体做法——科学家联手合作,这正是答案理由。 

 【替换】 they came together at the first Global Conference on Agricultural Research ↔ The cooperation of the world's agricultural scientists 具体行为概括为合作 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 的 new farming techniques 让人联想第二段讲新品种/新技术,但录音从未说科学家"鼓励农民采纳新技术";被表扬的是科学家联手开会,A 是无中生有的理由。 
 B) 偷换概念 B 盗用录音 change research agendas(调整研究议程)制造熟悉感,但录音说调整议程是"为满足穷国农民需求",B 却说成 aligning their research with advances in farming technology(让研究对齐农业技术进步),偷换了目的。  借用原文：change research agendas to help meet the needs of farmers in poorer nations 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 借第四段末 policy-makers 原词诱选,但录音说的是 these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers(除非获得政策制定者更多支持,计划才能见效)——这是"尚缺的条件",而非科学家已做、被表扬的事,方向错位。  借用原文：these plans will not bear fruit unless they get considerably more support from policy-makers

questions.prompt: What makes China exceptional in comparison with the rest of the world?
options: Rapid transition to become a food exporter.
Substantial funding in agricultural research.
Quick rise to become a leading grain producer.
Assumption of humanitarian responsibilities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What makes China exceptional in comparison with the rest of the world? 

 【翻译】 与世界其他地区相比,是什么使中国与众不同? 
 A)  快速转型成为粮食出口国。 
 B)  农业研究方面的大量资金投入。 
 C)  迅速崛起成为主要粮食生产国。 
 D)  承担人道主义责任。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Substantial funding in agricultural research. 
 【定位】 P5 The big exception is China, where spending has far surpassed other countries over the past decade. 
 最大的例外是中国,过去十年里中国的(农业研究)支出远远超过其他国家。 

 【信号】 The big exception 例外信号 。第五段 The big exception is China 用 exception 与题干 exceptional 直接呼应,紧跟 spending has far surpassed other countries 交代了中国例外之处——研究支出远超他国,这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 spending has far surpassed other countries ↔ Substantial funding in agricultural research 支出远超=大量投入 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 录音讲中国 transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology(转为向穷国供应相关科技),A 把 supplier/transition 误读成 transition to become a food exporter(转为粮食出口国),录音从没说中国成为粮食出口国。  借用原文：transition to become the key supplier of relevant science and technology to poorer countries 

 C) 未提及 C 的 leading grain producer(领先产粮国)蹭了全篇"粮食/农业"的主题词,但录音讲中国例外是因为研究"支出"远超他国,完全没说中国是产粮大国,无中生有。 
 D) 张冠李戴 D 盗用录音 humanitarian responsibility 原词,但那句是 developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too(发达国家也有人道责任),主语是"发达国家",不是中国;D 把这责任安到中国头上,张冠李戴。  借用原文：developed countries have a humanitarian responsibility too
